:::{#thm-reed-solomon-distance}
#### Reed--Solomon codes meet the Singleton bound

The [Reed--Solomon code](#def-reed-solomon-code)
is an $[n, k, n - k + 1]_q$ [linear code](#def-linear-code).

:::

::: {.proof}
The map $m \mapsto E(m)$ is linear, because $f_{m + m'} = f_m + f_{m'}$
and $f_{\lambda m} = \lambda f_m$ for every scalar $\lambda$.
If $m \ne 0$, then $f_m$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $k - 1$,
so it has at most $k - 1$ roots,
and $E(m)$ has at least $n - k + 1 \ge 1$ nonzero entries.
So $E$ is one-to-one, the codewords form a $k$-dimensional subspace,
and by @rem-linear-code-weight the minimum distance is at least $n - k + 1$.
The [Singleton bound](#thm-singleton-bound) says it is at most $n - k + 1$.

:::
